artifact: bounded read of one supplied description
scope: Local method check on one invented teaching sentence supplied by the requester. It is not a medicine evaluation, not an evidence review and not a statement about any real cohort. No retrieval was performed, no source exists behind the sentence, and nothing here may be read as clinical or regulatory acceptance.

input.text: One unblinded convenience cohort of 20 adults reported symptom improvement in 12 participants; 3 reported rash. There was no comparator or adjudication.
input.origin: invented teaching material supplied with the request

reportedDesign.reported_design_basis: The sentence calls itself a convenience cohort. That is the design label it reports; nothing beyond the sentence corroborates it.
reportedDesign.why_assignment_is_unknown: The sentence does not state how exposure or treatment was assigned, by whom, or on what basis, and it names no intervention. The word cohort does not establish investigator-assigned treatment, and convenience sampling states how participants were found rather than how treatment was assigned. Assignment therefore stays unknown and the design is not restated as interventional.

blinding.detail: The sentence states the cohort was unblinded and names no role that was blinded.

sampling.detail: Convenience sampling is stated. Selection for the sample is neither described nor controlled.

comparator.detail: The sentence states there was no comparator.

outcome_adjudication.detail: The sentence states there was no adjudication.

observedCounts.how_read: Read exactly as the sentence states them: counts out of the reported total. Symptom improvement has no stated definition, instrument, time point or assessor; rash has no stated definition, severity, timing or relation to any exposure.
notes: A count of improvement in an uncontrolled, unblinded convenience cohort of this size is not an effect estimate: with no comparator there is no contrast to estimate.
No percentage in this file may be read as a rate over a defined population, a background rate, or a risk difference.
The two counts are not adjudicated and not independently verified, and no participant-level data exist.

domains.rationale: The sentence reports that 12 of 20 participants improved. With no comparator, no stated outcome definition and no adjudication, no effect can be estimated and no conclusion about benefit follows.

The sentence reports that 3 of 20 participants had rash. A single uncontrolled count of one event term, with no definition, timing, severity or follow-up completeness, cannot support a harm rate, a comparison with a background rate, or an attribution.
Nothing about setting, eligibility, exposure, follow-up or case mix is stated, so there is no basis for judging to whom any of it would apply.

No named certainty framework was applied, no traceable full text exists, and the risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication-bias judgements a formal rating requires were not made. A narrative impression is not a certainty assessment.
No price, jurisdiction, perspective, time horizon or cost data is present, and none was invented to fill the gap.

formal_certainty_reason: Certainty requires a named framework plus explicit domain judgements on traceable full-text evidence. The input is one sentence with no source behind it, so nothing is rated and no rating is implied by design alone.

quantitativeScoring.reason: No quantitative score was requested and no evaluation domains, item definitions, scales, weights, missing-data rules or scoring policy version were supplied, so no score is computed or shown. Missing evidence is not scored as zero.

recommendation_reason: No recommendation is made. The input supports no benefit-harm judgement, and a recommendation would have to be invented rather than derived from it.

causality.detail: The sentence describes co-occurrence of an exposure context and outcomes at most; it states no comparator in time or between groups and no adjudication. Nothing here supports a causal statement, and none is made.
